plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU, MSFU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration limit.
This plan prioritizes safety and reduces overall portfolio risk significantly.
Maintain a large cash buffer for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged positions and maintaining a cash buffer. Returns will be lower, but volatility is also greatly reduced.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to reduce overall leverage and concentration.
Buy AMZN at 4% as a quality tech addition from the scanner's strong setups.
This plan balances risk and growth, aiming for a more diversified portfolio.
Maintain a cash buffer of around 10%.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality name. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns compared to aggressive modes.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to press working assets.
Buy AMZN at 5% as a high-scoring scanner setup to add quality tech.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer of around 5%.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for ~4%/month, stretching for growth with increased leverage and concentration. It carries significantly higher drawdown risk, amplified by leveraged ETFs' daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell all high-beta and leveraged names (METU, SOXL, MSFU, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to near zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for steady monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes reliable income and low drawdown over growth.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on steady monthly distributions and capital preservation. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
